gen-dafont-existence-merriweather: Existence bends its letters like a single length of wire, with wide porthole counters and terminals cut short of the bowl. Wire-bent shapes make the headline; Merriweather, a serif, handles the stocky, soft-edged text.
gen-dafont-existence-mulish: Wide, porthole-like counters give Existence its industrial look, with terminals cut well short of each bowl. Mulish below stays uniform in stroke, leaving all the attention to the heading.
gen-dafont-existence-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, fills each line with a dominant middle zone and generous open throats. Above it, Existence adds slim pipe-cleaner joins and porthole counters, industrial and modern.
gen-dafont-fenwick-poppins: Poppins arrives loose and rope-curved, with no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye and a tall, sturdy lowercase. Poppins does the sturdy, modern work while Fenwick supplies graceful, literary turns.
gen-dafont-franchise-bitter: Strong and clean, Franchise stands tall with narrow ascenders and jammed-together characters, its c tips pulled well apart. Bitter, a slab-serif, supplies grounded footing through its huge lowercase eyes.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-nunito: Approachable Nunito rounds its lowercase bowls big and lets terminals finish well clear of the stem. And Franchise, bent like a single wire, stands tall and tight above it.
gen-dafont-franchise-fs-quicksand: Quicksand, a sans-serif, blows tall lowercase bowls like glass bulbs, each terminal finishing well clear of the stem. A touch more size helps it hold up beside tightly packed Franchise.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-abyssinica-sil: Abyssinica SIL has a quiet shift in line weight like brushed watercolor, with curves that thicken gently at the shoulders. And a larger size for Franchise lets its unshaded strokes stand apart.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-cambo: Cambo, a serif, keeps a short step from lowercase top to capital top and a modest thick-thin rhythm across each word. Franchise does the loud, uniform diagonals; Cambo does the quiet bookish refinement.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-fanwood-text: Tightly jammed characters with tall small letters mark Franchise, whose curves hold their weight at the shoulders. Fanwood Text, a serif, adds a gentle swell you feel more than see.
